meta.title: Hindi C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hindi → English (see the Hindi, recall the meaning) and English → Hindi (see an English meaning, recall the Hindi). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express themselves fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Hindi, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 121 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — academic work and method, law and the state, politics and administration, business and finance, science and medicine, the environment and geography, literature, religion and philosophy, history, the finer emotions, and the verbs, adjectives and discourse markers of complex argument — and the other 1379 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hindi, taken from a frequency list built from Hindi Wikipedia, web pages, Twitter and Reddit (the film and television subtitles that rank the lower levels have no ranking left at this depth) and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Devanagari with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's own (ā ī ū for the long vowels, a tilde or a dot for nasalisation: khānā, ma͠i), so the deck can be studied before the script is fluent; the Hindi Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. The 1029 nouns show their gender, masculine or feminine, which every adjective, postposition and past-tense verb agrees with, and their plural; the 81 verbs show their past forms, where Hindi verbs are irregular, and behind the All forms fold their present, future, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 288 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 65 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Hindi list of wordfreq 3.1.1 by Robyn Speer, built from Wikipedia, ParaCrawl, Twitter and Reddit (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
